A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GenDA and the same Bristol urban-flow study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite additions and substantial reformatting in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction experiments on CFD-derived urban flows, including baseline comparisons, sensor-placement tests, and guidance and observation-density analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, withheld-sensor evaluation, probabilistic scores, and a multiscale architecture ablation.

M1.justification: GenDA retains its two-level graph architecture, EDM training objective, sensor-dropout conditioning, and classifier-free guidance sampling. The single-mesh variant is introduced as an ablation; explanations of known wind direction and possible off-mesh observations do not establish changes to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Bristol dataset, six altitude slices, 360 wind directions per slice, and random, cloud, and trajectory sensing configurations. The new withheld-sensor and probabilistic evaluations reuse this coverage and change evaluation procedures rather than the represented domain or reconstruction task.

E2.justification: V3 adds POD-3DVar and the directly conditioned stochastic diffusion baseline MultiMesh-VP to Table 1 and Figure 5, substantially broadening the comparison methods. Figure 10 also adds LCSVD and these two methods to the component-wise comparison, which in v2 contains only MGN, MS-MGN, and GenDA.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 introduces evaluation restricted to withheld sensor nodes; Appendix C.2 specifies providing 25% of a fixed network's measurements and withholding 75%. V3 also introduces ensemble CRPS, marginal-distribution Wasserstein evaluation, and the single-mesh control. The existing altitude split and GenDA training and sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's guidance, density, and sensing-strategy analyses, v3 directly tests the multiscale hierarchy through SM-GenDA in Appendix C.3. It also adds withheld-measurement diagnostics, ensemble and distribution analyses, and a density-specific guidance sweep showing instability with strong guidance at higher observation counts.

E5.justification: V2 reports variation in reconstruction metrics across cases and sensor placements. V3 additionally defines and reports finite-ensemble CRPS to assess predictive distributions, and Table 3 specifies aggregation over 60 evaluations. These are new statistical reporting practices; the PDFs do not establish increased independent training runs or specify the numerical ensemble size.

E6.justification: The existing scores in Tables 1 and 2 are retained, but v3 adds substantial baseline, withheld-sensor, guidance, probabilistic, and ablation results in Tables 1, 3, and 5–8. Figure 10 also changes GenDA's component RRMSE values from 0.123/0.278 to 0.124/0.283 for the same stated 253-degree, 1662-observation example. These are reported value revisions, not evidence of an overall method improvement or decline.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 introduces the finite-ensemble CRPS definition in Equation 22 for the new probabilistic evaluation. The posterior, guidance, graph-network, training, and original metric equations remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V3 qualifies generalization as transfer within the studied urban-flow distribution and softens direct 3D extensibility to an extension requiring future validation. Its contribution statements also include stochastic diffusion comparisons and withheld-sensor tests, while retaining the central GenDA contribution and headline performance claims.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly discusses the single-neighborhood, steady-2D validation boundary and the absence of hard PDE, mass-conservation, and boundary-condition enforcement. It adds deployment validation and calibration requirements, interprets the hierarchy ablation, and revises excessive-guidance failure from overfitting sparse or noisy measurements to over-correction especially at higher sensor densities.

D1.justification: V3 adds an implementation repository link and Appendix B.4 describing baseline observation encoding, POD-3DVar's covariance-weighted reconstruction, and MultiMesh-VP conditioning. The existing GenDA hyperparameters, hardware, training budget, and preprocessing details are retained. The PDFs establish the added access information, not the repository's operational availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds Song et al. (2021) and Vermeulen and Heemink (2006) to position the new diffusion and variational assimilation comparisons. The broader related-work narrative is retained; the Amorós-Trepat citation's publication update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: The main narrative sequence and most method and training prose remain intact. V3 makes localized rewrites to the introduction, comparisons, and conclusions, adds an Impact Statement and new experimental subsections, renumbers retained Appendix C material, and updates author and affiliation text.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout. V3 adds five tables, expands Table 1, and redraws Figures 5 and 10 with additional comparator rows and adjusted color scales. Other figure images are retained with placement or sizing changes.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses important gaps in v2's empirical support through a stochastic comparator, a direct multiscale ablation, withheld-sensor evaluation, and ensemble scoring (Tables 1, 3, 6, and 8). Its explicit applicability and physical-consistency limitations also better align claims with demonstrated evidence. Ensemble size and baseline hyperparameters remain incompletely documented, but the stronger validation and more restrained claims provide a substantial net quality improvement.
